# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

This step sets the project directory and loads the raw SRA metadata.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

# (1) Setting working directory
project_id <- "PRJNA321534"

base_dir <- "E:/工作区/VSCode/RNAproject/collect_metadata_respon/project"
setwd(file.path(base_dir, project_id))

# (2) Loading raw SRA metadata file
sra_file <- "SraRunTable.csv"
initial_meta <- read.csv(sra_file, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

# Step 2: Data Overview

First, you need to get an overview of the data, which includes two steps: reading the article and reading the initial metadata. This step is very IMPORTANT!

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# (1) Read the article in the following order: abstract, the beginning of the results section, and the methods.
# Paper summary used for this project:
# - Title: Oral microbiota of periodontal health and disease and their changes after nonsurgical periodontal therapy
# - Study design: oral microbiome comparison across periodontal health and chronic periodontitis, with post-treatment follow-up for a subset of diseased subjects
# - Sample size from the paper: 238 saliva and subgingival plaque samples from 21 periodontally healthy adults and 48 adults with chronic periodontitis
# - Longitudinal subset from Methods/Table 1: 19 diseased subjects were sampled again at least 4 weeks after nonsurgical periodontal therapy
# - Sample groups from the paper: HP/HS for healthy plaque/saliva, D1P/D1S for diseased pre-treatment plaque/saliva, and D2P/D2S for diseased post-treatment plaque/saliva
# - Sequencing from the paper: 16S rRNA V4 region amplified with primers targeting base positions 515-806 and sequenced on Illumina MiSeq
# - Supplementary Table S1 (41396_2017_37_MOESM2_ESM.docx) provides the 515F/806R primer set in indexed form
# - Supplementary Table S2 (41396_2017_37_MOESM3_ESM.docx) provides cohort-level demographics and sample counts, not per-sample annotations
# - Geography from the paper affiliations and recruitment site: Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry of USC, Los Angeles, California, USA

# (2) IMPORTANT: MUST go through each column of initial_meta
head(initial_meta, 10)
colnames(initial_meta)
table(initial_meta$sample_site)
table(initial_meta$Diseased)
table(initial_meta$gender)
table(initial_meta$treatment)
table(initial_meta$subject)
table(initial_meta$Host)
table(initial_meta$Instrument)
table(initial_meta$`Sample Name`)
# Raw SRA fields already usable for target metadata:
# - sample_id: Run
# - subject_id: subject
# - age: AGE
# - sex: gender
# - site: sample_site
# - public_time: ReleaseDate
# - status / longitudinal structure: Diseased + treatment + subject
# Raw SRA fields that are not sufficient alone:
# - country: geo_loc_name_country is uncalculated for all rows
# - platform / sequencing_region / pcr_primers: must be confirmed from paper and supplements
# Supplementary files worth using in this project:
# - S1 for sequencing primer names
# - S2 for cohort-level age/sex/sample-count cross-checks
# All 238 rows are human oral samples, with sample_site limited to Plaque and Saliva.
# subject is the stable participant identifier; Sample Name encodes site and treatment state rather than a reusable subject ID.
```

# Step 3: Removing Control and Non-human Samples

First, we need to remove control samples(including both negative controls and positive controls) and non-human samples.

```{r}
# (1) Parameter setup
control_column <- ""
control_keywords <- c()

species_column <- "Host"
unique(initial_meta[[species_column]])
non_human_keywords <- c()

# (2) Remove controls and non-human samples. DO NOT need to modify code in this part, just run it.
n_samples <- nrow(initial_meta)
# Control evaluation
if (length(control_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(control_column) || control_column == "") {
    stop("Error: control_keywords provided but control_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(control_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", control_column))
  }

  control_pattern <- paste(control_keywords, collapse = "|")
  control_text <- initial_meta[[control_column]]
  is_control <- grepl(control_pattern, control_text)

} else {
  is_control <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Non-human evaluation
if (length(non_human_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(species_column) || species_column == "") {
    stop("Error: non_human_keywords provided but species_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(species_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", species_column))
  }

  non_human_pattern <- paste(non_human_keywords, collapse = "|")
  species_text <- initial_meta[[species_column]]
  is_non_human <- grepl(non_human_pattern, species_text)
} else {
  is_non_human <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Execute removal
samples_to_remove <- is_control | is_non_human
initial_meta <- initial_meta[!samples_to_remove, ]

cat("Initial samples counts:", n_samples, "\n")
cat("Removed control samples:", sum(is_control), "\n")
cat("Removed non-human samples:", sum(is_non_human), "\n")
cat("Total samples removed ", sum(samples_to_remove), "\n")
cat("Remaining samples after Step 2:", nrow(initial_meta), "\n")
```

# Step 4: Creating a Uniform Metadata Template

This step converts the raw SRA table into the standard metadata format used in our meta-analysis.

```{r}
metadata <- data.frame(
  bioproject = initial_meta$BioProject,
  sample_id = initial_meta$Run,
  subject_id = initial_meta$subject,
  age = as.numeric(initial_meta$AGE),
  age_info = NA_character_,
  bmi = NA_real_,
  raw_sex = initial_meta$gender,
  sex = "pending",
  sequencing_region = "V4",
  platform = "Illumina MiSeq",
  country = "USA",
  raw_site = initial_meta$sample_site,
  site = "pending",
  site_group = "pending",
  public_time = sub("T.*$", "", initial_meta$ReleaseDate),
  pcr_primers = "515F/806R",
  title = "Oral microbiota of periodontal health and disease and their changes after nonsurgical periodontal therapy",
  disease_study = "yes",
  raw_status = initial_meta$Diseased,
  status = "pending",
  matched_samples = "pending",
  raw_treatment = initial_meta$treatment,
  is_time_series = "pending",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Source notes for non-obvious fields:
# - subject_id uses the SraRunTable subject column because Sample Name mixes site and treatment encodings, while subject is the participant identifier reused across rows.
# - age comes directly from AGE, while Supplementary Table S2 is used only as a cohort-level cross-check, so age_info remains NA.
# - sequencing_region and platform come from the paper abstract/methods, not from SRA technical columns.
# - country is set to USA from the USC recruitment site because geo_loc_name_country is uncalculated in SRA.
# - pcr_primers uses the 515F/806R shorthand supported by Supplementary Table S1 (41396_2017_37_MOESM2_ESM.docx).
# - site, status, matched_samples, and is_time_series are resolved from raw SRA columns plus the paper design in Step 5, with Supplementary Table S2 cross-checking the cohort counts.
# - Treatment follow-up in an intervention study is not labeled as is_time_series in this project.
metadata$public_time <- as.Date(metadata$public_time)
```

# Step 5: Manually solving pending issues

This step involves two parts: (1) handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix, and next (2) handle the `site_group` and `matched_samples` columns.

```{r}
# (1) Handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix.
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    sex = case_when(
      raw_sex == "male" ~ "M",
      raw_sex == "female" ~ "F",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    site = case_when(
      raw_site == "Plaque" ~ "subgingival plaque",
      raw_site == "Saliva" ~ "saliva",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    status = case_when(
      raw_status == "n" ~ "HC",
      raw_status == "y" ~ "chronic periodontitis",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
# Plaque is promoted to subgingival plaque because the paper Methods specify subgingival sampling with sterile paper points.
# Diseased rows remain chronic periodontitis after treatment because D2P/D2S are reevaluation samples from the periodontitis cohort.
```

```{r}
# (2) Filling the 'site_group', 'matched_samples', and 'is_time_series' columns
unique(metadata$site)
Oral_site = c("saliva", "subgingival plaque")
Gut_site = c("feces")

metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(site_group = case_when(
    site %in% Oral_site ~ "oral",
    site %in% Gut_site ~ "gut",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  ))

subject_sample_counts <- ave(metadata$subject_id, metadata$subject_id, FUN = length)
metadata$matched_samples <- ifelse(subject_sample_counts > 1, "yes", "no")

metadata$is_time_series <- "no"
# matched_samples is yes for all rows because every subject contributes multiple oral samples.
# Post-treatment follow-up in this intervention study is tracked through matched_samples and treatment labels, not as is_time_series.
```

```{r}
# (3) check if there is pending value in metadata. If there is pending value, go on modify the metadata.
has_pending <- function(col) {
  if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) {
    any(col == "pending", na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    FALSE
  }
}

any_pending_value <- any(sapply(metadata, has_pending))

if (!any_pending_value) {
  message("Good! No cell contains the value 'pending'.")
} else {
  pending_cols <- names(metadata)[sapply(metadata, has_pending)]
  message("Columns containing 'pending': ", paste(pending_cols, collapse = ", "))
  message("Please continue to resolve these pending columns!")
}
```

# Step 6: Visualize the Metadata

This step makes a quick set of plots for checking the distribution of key metadata fields.

```{r}
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-bioproject, -sample_id, -subject_id, -title)

create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  continuous_vars <- c("age", "bmi")

  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (col %in% continuous_vars && is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
        labs(title = col, x = col, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }

  return(plots)
}

plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p <- plot_grid(plots$age,
               plots$bmi,
               plots$sex,
               plots$site,
               plots$site_group,
               plots$sequencing_region,
               plots$platform,
               plots$country,
               plots$status,
               plots$matched_samples,
               ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("Metadata_Summary.png")
```

# Step 7: Sort and export the metadata

This step saves the cleaned metadata table as the final `metadata_v2.csv` file.

```{r}
fixed_cols <- c("bioproject", "sample_id", "subject_id", "age", "age_info",
                "bmi", "sex", "platform", "sequencing_region", "pcr_primers",
                "country", "site", "site_group", "disease_study", "status",
                "title", "public_time", "matched_samples", "is_time_series")
metadata <- metadata %>%
  select(all_of(fixed_cols), starts_with("raw_"))

write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata_v2.csv", quote = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
```
